title: I'll Turn Out Fine
author: William Saville
content:
Far off looks,
I breathe through teeth,
Narrowed eyes,
Inward I weep.
They call me brave,
They call me strong,
I don't want to be either,
I just want to belong.
I want to be safe,
I want to be me,
The broken and the healed,
For all to see.
So many paths,
Behind and ahead,
But I never know,
Which path will leave me dead.
My choices aren't my own,
When I have to play their game,
I choose survival,
When it goes wrong I take the blame.
Smallest sounds,
Like a thunderous crack,
Hair stands on end,
Fear is the only thing I don't lack.
Hyper-vigilance has become,
My longest standing friend,
The loneliness and agony,
Something on which to depend.
If I can trust nothing else,
I know in my heart,
That my suffering is not over,
But at least it isn't the start.
When you are used to pain,
And the blows fall on bruised humanity,
Bruised flesh, heart, soul, and mind,
Find comfort in calamity.
When inordinate truths become commonplace,
And pain becomes the norm,
A lifted arm to block,
Becomes an arm more easily torn.
So I give rise to my chin,
Take the blows with defiance,
I get back up when I fall,
And with darkness I make an alliance.
Take that darkness and hopelessness,
And fill it with my light,
Join others who can do the same,
Hold their hands as we fight.
Love harder and with more passion,
Than society says is natural or okay,
Taking every moment as precious,
With every act of love we display.
Through the eyes of a battered child,
Who desperately longed for affection,
Through the sobs of a battered woman,
Who became a man in his reflection.
My heart and mind have endured,
So much pain and misery,
But to remain the man I am,
I'd relive it again happily.
I'd rather suffer as myself,
Than have died or endured as a lie,
Rather have my broken bones and family,
Than to never try.
Those who love me now,
Love me as I shine,
Battered and bruised maybe,
But one day I'll turn out fine.
